title: kith-chat: old_state/new_state captured inside lock scope prevents newState race condition
description: ChatContactSetHandler, ChatSetHandler, and MessageSetHandler all capture old_state before the first write and new_state after the last write, both inside the same Mutex lock scope as the write. This prevents a concurrent Peer/deliver from slipping in between the write and the state read, which would produce a newState that under-reports this Set's changes (causing clients to miss the concurrent change on their next /changes call). A contributor might suggest reading state outside the lock for simplicity, but that would reintroduce the race. The comment in ChatContactSetHandler (lines 199-210) documents the invariant and why it matters.
